2. Execute an SEO Process

Learn how to execute SEO processes effectively with these expert-backed resources. Whether you want to conduct an SEO audit, or improve your existing strategy, this comprehensive guide brings together actionable resources, templates, and real-world tips from leading professionals.

Executing an effective SEO process requires more than just keyword research—it demands a systematic approach that covers strategy development, goal setting, performance measurement, and stakeholder buy-in. From conducting thorough SEO audits to establishing measurable objectives and creating compelling reports, each phase plays a crucial role in driving organic growth.

Start building, measuring, and reporting on SEO success using these proven tactics designed for marketers, website owners, and anyone ready to advance their SEO skills.

Tips from Experienced SEO Professionals to Execute an SEO Process

Gain practical insights from experienced professionals on how to execute SEO processes effectively. These expert tips go beyond theory, offering actionable advice to help you avoid common pitfalls and achieve measurable results—whether you’re just starting to learn SEO or looking to refine your approach as a seasoned marketer.

Before defining an SEO strategy, learn what the company's global and marketing strategy is. So that you can work on your SEO goals. Once you have the goals it is easier (from my point of view) to define the KPIs you want to measure and make an SEO strategy.

It’s important to present the strategy in a simple format to stakeholders and include goals, metrics and tactics at a high level. A simple table can do the trick. Having everything clearly stated in one place helps people understand and support your strategy.

Always remember that your job as a staff member, agency, or freelance is to make your boss/client look good. Focus on things that will help them, not just what you want to do.

Measure metrics that have an impact on the bottom line for the business in order to help you and the business focus on the right work to improve sales and not just what SEO usually prioritises.

Check with your direct client to understand what their OKRs or KPIs are and structure a set of reports for them directly, as well as one for the business that helps them present to higher ups. That way you and your direct report can have a more detailed look at the metrics.

When it comes to creating process, you should record tasks and steps in such a way that anyone, could step in and replace you. That can sound a bit scary because you don’t want to leave yourself vulnerable to being replaced, but, you won’t!

Eventually, if you’re ambitious, you will crave a higher role within a company or as a consultant you’ll want to keep your eyes on what’s next, looking for the next strategic move rather than repeating the same old tasks. A well thought out step-by-step process means you can easily bring someone else in when you’re ready for it.

Best practices for creating process include recording yourself doing a task that you do often. Add a little instruction as you go. Get into the habit of doing this well before you need support. It’s great practice and for freelancers/consultants or small agencies it’ll help you scale faster. When you’ve got your recording, have the first person who works from it (maybe a junior team member or VA) watch the process, do the work and have them create a step by step process in writing. This way you have the written process to support the video and you flesh out the process as needed.

Plus, you can use it to check your new team members understanding and identify where they may need a bit more training.
Zoe Ashbridge

When it comes to executing an SEO strategy for a client, you should always start by getting to know that client first. What are their business/marketing goals? What are they hoping to accomplish with SEO? It also helps to understand your client’s familiarity level with SEO. This will help you be able to explain your strategy and tactics to the client in a way that they will best understand. Once you understand the client’s vision, it’s time to align them with clearly defined goals. These goals should be realistic, data-driven, align with the business’s goals, and quantifiable. Even after these are set, it’s important to revisit them and determine if they are still the best course of action or if it’s time to pivot.

When measuring SEO process execution success, It’s best to look beyond rankings and focus on holistic metrics that align with the business objectives.
Instead of relying solely on keyword rankings, consider tracking organic traffic, conversion rates, engagement metrics, the backlink profile and keyword performance.
That way, you get a comprehensive picture of the impact of your SEO efforts on things that matter to the overall business performance like user engagement, visibility and conversions.
These are the holistic metrics that can better help you make data-driven decisions, better optimize your strategy, and demonstrate the real value of SEO in driving meaningful results.
Silvia Gituto
X Linkedin Threads
When executing your SEO strategy, break big goals into smaller achievable milestones. Doing this will help you stay motivated and track your progress. Create a reasonable roadmap with incremental milestones that leads you to your ultimate goal. This approach allows you to enjoy your SEO journey, celebrate small wins, make necessary adjustments and maintain a continuous momentum.

The SEO Process Execution FAQ

The steps to follow when executing an SEO process depend on the nature, context and goal of the project, however, in general, an SEO process tends to start with a keyword and competition research and an SEO audit -including technical configuration, content optimization, and link profile analysis- to establish an SEO strategy that achieves the expected goals. After the SEO strategy and goals are set, and the viability of actions validated by stakeholders, the SEO process implementation and monitorization starts, and can take place for months on an ongoing basis, due to the long term nature of SEO. 

This depends on the nature of the Website, however, when working in SEO processes with clients, the SEO specialist will work with Web and digital marketing specialists dedicated to the Website, such as Web developers and content writers who will execute the SEO recommendations established by the SEO specialists. 

This will depend on the scope of work, how well optimized is the Website, as well as the complexity and resources when implementing the SEO recommendations, and the time it takes search engines to take into account the implemented actions. Having said this, SEO is usually a long-term process, that usually takes months or years. 

The most common challenge when executing an SEO process is the lack or scarcity of resources and flexibility to implement technical and content actions. This is mainly due to buy-in struggles with decision-makers and lack of alignment and support from stakeholders. This is why it’s fundamental to show the potential impact and value of the recommended SEO actions toward the site business, as well as setting the right expectations and clear communication that decision makers and stakeholders can understand. 

Success can be measured using KPIs like improved keyword rankings, organic search traffic growth, and ultimately, an increase in conversions and revenue coming from organic search traffic as an outcome of the SEO process. Regular reporting and goal tracking are key to evaluating performance.

SEO strategy defines the plan—target keywords, audiences, and goals—while SEO execution is about operationalizing that plan through specific tasks, workflows, and measurement systems to drive results.

Executing SEO effectively means putting your SEO strategy into action through structured processes like audits, goal setting, performance tracking, and reporting. It involves aligning SEO efforts with business objectives and ensuring all activities contribute to measurable growth.
